messages.subject: memory management in INLA
parts:
Dear INLA authors,

I have a couple of questions regarding memory management in INLA. I have a fairly sizeable model (leads to a graph with ~1e6 nodes) that I'm trying to push through INLA at the moment, but I keep running into memory problems. The machine I'm using has 4 CPUs, with 6 cores each, and 64GB of RAM. Although memory consumption during the initial optimisation is in the 15% range, it balloons up afterwards until INLA crashes with a malloc error. I'm guessing this has to do with parallelisation, is that correct? Is there any way to limit parallelisation to avoid that problem? Thanks a lot, and thanks for the great software!

Best,

Simon Barthelmé

On Thu, 2012-02-09 at 02:20 -0800, Simon Barthelmé wrote:
> Dear INLA authors,
>
> I have a couple of questions regarding memory management in INLA. I
> have a fairly sizeable model (leads to a graph with ~1e6 nodes) that
> I'm trying to push through INLA at the moment, but I keep running into
> memory problems. The machine I'm using has 4 CPUs, with 6 cores each,
> and 64GB of RAM. Although memory consumption during the initial
> optimisation is in the 15% range, it balloons up afterwards until INLA
> crashes with a malloc error. I'm guessing this has to do with
> parallelisation, is that correct? Is there any way to limit
> parallelisation to avoid that problem? Thanks a lot, and thanks for
> the great software!

the problem is that you have to divide the RAM on the number of cpus
you're using.

so I suggest you run with

inla(..., num.threads=X)

and increase X from 2, say, until it crash.

if you run into problems still; we can give you access to a linux-server
here with 12cpu and 96Gb ram to run your model.
